title: Tiered checkout discount
topic: Off-by-one range and shadowed branch order
blurb: A checkout calculator with two classic boundary & branch bugs.
prompt: Spec: sum all item prices, apply 25% off for orders $500+ or 10% off for orders $100+, and return the final total. Review the AI's code.

segments.label: L2
segments.text: subtotal = sum(prices[i] for i in range(len(prices) - 1))

conclusion: AI summary: Sums all prices and applies 10% off at $100+ or 25% off at $500+.

flaws.corrupted: subtotal = sum(prices[i] for i in range(len(prices) - 1))

diagnosis_choices.label: Off-by-one: `range(len(prices) - 1)` stops before the last index, silently dropping the last item.
Python's `sum()` cannot accept a generator expression.

fix_choices.label: Use `range(1, len(prices))` to include the last item.
Use `range(len(prices) + 1)` so the last index is included.

flaws.explanation: `range(n)` generates `0 .. n-1`. Subtracting 1 cuts off the final element of `prices` (and gives 0 for a single-item cart!).
flaws.why_tempting: People remember 'last index is `len - 1`' and forget that `range()` already excludes its stop value.
flaws.catch_rule: Test loops on a 1-element list: if `range(len(xs) - 1)` runs 0 times, it's off by one.

practice.problem: Which elements of `xs = [10, 20, 30]` does `xs[i]` visit for `i in range(len(xs) - 1)`?

flaws.original: if subtotal >= 500: discount = 0.25  # check the higher threshold first

diagnosis_choices.label: Unreachable branch: any `subtotal >= 500` already matched `if subtotal >= 100` on L3.
`elif` cannot compare the same variable twice in Python.
`>= 500` should be `> 500` because $500 orders only get 10%.

fix_choices.label: Check the stricter condition first: `if subtotal >= 500:` (0.25), then `elif subtotal >= 100:` (0.10).
Remove the `else` branch so Python evaluates both `if` and `elif`.
Swap `0.10` and `0.25` while keeping the same threshold order.

flaws.explanation: In an `if / elif` chain, only the first true branch runs. Because every number `>= 500` is also `>= 100`, the 25% tier is dead code.
flaws.why_tempting: Listing tiers from smallest ($100) to largest ($500) reads naturally in English, even though `if/elif` requires the reverse.
flaws.catch_rule: In threshold `if/elif` chains, always order conditions from most restrictive to least restrictive (highest to lowest for `>=`).
flaws.hint: Trace a $600 order through lines 3–6: which branch actually executes?

practice.problem: In `if score >= 60: g='D' elif score >= 90: g='A'`, what grade does 95 get?

clean_conclusion: All items are summed and orders at $500+ properly receive the 25% tier.
